narrative_purpose: Shows the slime mould solving a network-design problem with no brain: from a sprawling exploratory mass it prunes to an efficient transport web that mirrors an optimised rail map — brainless competence through pure local feedback, the headline case that breaks the 'brainless means stupid' link.
subject: A two-stage comparison on one plate. Left: a single yellow-cyan slime-mould mass sprawling messily over a dark plate dotted with small food specks, branches reaching everywhere. Right: the same organism after pruning, now a clean efficient network of glowing tubes connecting the same specks in an elegant rail-map-like layout, redundant branches gone.
scene: A dark wet culture plate seen from directly above, food specks scattered in a city-like constellation across both halves.
camera: A flat top-down view of the plate, both stages side by side.
light: The living tubes are the light source — dim and diffuse on the left sprawl, bright and confident along the pruned efficient network on the right.
palette: Void-indigo plate, living-teal and Pandora-cyan glow in the organism, a faint warm amber on the food specks so the nodes read.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, organic.
detail_level: Crisp on the tube networks of both stages; plate background flat and dark.
composition: Two stages left and right with a clear gap between them, dark margins for labels at top and bottom.
consistency_notes: Earth-science figure in the book's cool palette; left = messy exploration, right = pruned efficiency, the contrast obvious at a glance; keep dark margins for callouts.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no neon UI glow, no cartoon or anime style
